stem.text: Halogenoalkanes react with hot ethanolic potassium cyanide.
The reaction mechanism is either $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ or $\text{S}_\text{N}2$.

A.text: All secondary halogenoalkanes react by the $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism only.

B.text: Both the halogenoalkane and the cyanide ion are involved in the initial step of the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism.

C.text: Chloroethane reacts with cyanide ions by the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism only.

D.text: The $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism involves a short-lived negatively charged transition state.
